rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the suggestion that the Prophet turned toward the wealthy for their riches: the verse says the other man came striving and fearing, not that he was poor.
rows.anchor: وهو فاسد- هاهنا- لأن إقبال النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- لم يكن لثروتهم ومالهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، والكلبي، ومقاتل
rows.claim: They understand the man's striving as seeking God's pleasure and doing good that pleases Him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، والكلبي، ومقاتل (¬5): يسعى في الطلب لرضاء الله، والعمل في الخير وما يرضي الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He identifies the one who fears God as Ibn Umm Maktum.
rows.anchor: {وهو يخشى} الله عز وجل يعني ابن أم مكتوم

rows.speaker: الحسن، ومجاهد، وعطاء، والكلبي
rows.claim: They take the path as the way of good and evil, which God made known to humanity, as in 76:3.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن (¬6)، ومجاهد (¬7)، وعطاء (¬8) (¬9)، # والكلبي (¬1) (¬2): بين له سبيل الخير، والشر

rows.speaker: السدي، ومقاتل
rows.claim: They interpret it as God bringing the child out of the womb and guiding him to emerge from his mother's body.
rows.anchor: قال السدي (¬3)، ومقاتل (¬4): أي أخرجه من الرحم، وهداه للخروج من بطن أمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should consider how God created their food and made it a cause of life; the focus is its coming into existence, which invites reflection.
rows.anchor: أي فلينظر كيف خلق الله طعامه الذي جعله سببا لحياته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God split the earth open through vegetation.
rows.anchor: {ثم شققنا الأرض شقا} بالنبات (7)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grain refers to all kinds of grain that people use for nourishment.
rows.anchor: يعني الحبوب كلها مما يتغذى به

rows.speaker: أكثر أهل اللغة والتفسير
rows.claim: Most linguists and exegetes identify قضب as green alfalfa or wet fodder, called qat when dry; Meccans also use قضب, from repeated cutting. The source attributes this view to Abu Ubayda, al-Farra, al-Asma'i, Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, and Muqatil.
rows.anchor: أكثر أهل اللغة، والتفسير قالوا: القضب: الرطبة، وهي الفسفسة ما دامت خضراء، فإذا يبست فهو القت

rows.speaker: المبرد والحسن
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad, with al-Hasan, says قضب is fodder itself, named from being cut.
rows.anchor: قال المبرد: القضب هو العلف بعينه، وأصله من أنه يقضب، أي يقطع (¬7). وهو قول الحسن (¬8)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pages are the records of the children of Adam, which are spread open.
rows.anchor: يعني صحائف بني آدم نشرت

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says a person's record is folded at death, then opened on Judgment Day and handed to him open by the record-keeping angels.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: إن المرء إذا مات طويت صحيفة (¬2) أعماله، فإذا كان يوم القيامة نشرت

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators likewise explain that the records are spread open for reckoning.
rows.anchor: ونحو هذا قال المفسرون (¬4): نشرت للحساب

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar tells people to consult their diwan, explaining that pre-Islamic poetry contains the explanation of the Qur'an and the meanings of Arabic speech.
rows.anchor: فقال عمر رضي الله عنه: يا أيها الناس، عليكم بديوانكم لا يضل، قالوا: وما ديواننا؟ قال: شعر الجاهلية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas advises readers who cannot understand Qur'anic wording to seek its explanation in poetry, and he himself would cite poetry when asked about Qur'anic Arabic.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، أنه كان يسأل عن الشيء من عربية القرآن فينشد الشعر

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i calls Arabic scholars the jinn among humankind.
rows.anchor: سمعت الشافعي رضي الله عنه يقول: أصحاب العربية جن الإنس

rows.speaker: عبد الملك بن مروان
rows.claim: Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan urges people to learn Arabic, calling it visible refinement.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الملك بن مروان (¬5): تعلموا العربية فإنها المروءة الظاهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Few advance in any discipline without literature, Arabic metrics, and grammar; innovations and misleading desires arise from ignorance of Arabic.
rows.anchor: وقل من تقدم في علم من العلوم إلا بمعرفة الأدب، ومقاييس العربية، والنحو، وما حدثت البدع والأهواء المضلة إلا من الجهل بلغة العرب

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i says that most who became heretics in Iraq did so from ignorance of Arabic and its dialects.
rows.anchor: سمعت الشافعي يقول: عامة من تزندق (¬7) بالعراق لجهلهم بالعربية # ولغات العرب (¬1)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God comprehends all things, seen and unseen, public and secret, with knowledge untouched by doubt; 6:59 is cited as evidence for His knowledge of every detail.
rows.anchor: ويعلم ما في البر والبحر وما تسقط من ورقة إلا يعلمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows without thought, sees without eyes, creates without tools, speaks without a tongue or sound, wills without mental resolve, and governs and decrees without consultation or deliberation.
rows.anchor: من عالم لا بفكرة واجتهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger sent among the unlettered is from the noblest lineage, highest standing, best character, and most renowned parents.
rows.anchor: بعث في الأميين رسولا من أوسطهم نسبا، وأشرفهم حسبا، وأحسنهم أدبا، وأشهرهم أما وأبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He recites God's signs and answers falsehood with proofs; the clear revelation dispels doubt and disbelief and rescues people from misguidance and bewilderment.
rows.anchor: يتلو عليهم آياته، ويعارض أباطيلهم ببيناته، حتى انكشطت غشاوة الشك عن وجه اليقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an's Arabic raised the standing of its language, while its composition surpassed Arab eloquence; its audience failed to produce anything comparable despite their mastery of rhetoric.
rows.anchor: وجعله قرآنا عربيا فرفع به من شأن لغتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author had long planned a concise work on Qur'anic meanings, parsing, obscure points, and the reasons behind variant readings, and undertook it at the urging of serious scholars.
rows.anchor: فمنذ دهر تحدثني نفسي بأن أعلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He laments his era's neglect of learning and its pretenders, while affirming that a small number of genuine scholars remain virtuous and that knowledge retains its honor despite being shunned.
rows.anchor: لتوفر دواعي أهل زماننا على الجهل، وظهور رغباتهم عن العلم، الذي فيه شرف الدين والدنيا
